la:verb:obliviscor.html:
oblīviscor, lītus (archaic
inf. obliscier. ; ), 3, v. dep.
ob and livor, q. v.; livēre, to become dark; hence, to have the mind darkened, forget
, to forget; constr. with gen. of pers. and with gen. or acc. of thing; less freq. with inf. or a rel.clause (class.; cf. dedisco).
With gen. of person: vivorum memini, nec tamen Epicuri licet oblivisci,: nescio hercule, neque unde eam, neque quorsum eam; ita prorsum oblitus sum mei,I have so completely forgotten myself, been lost in thought,: regisque ducumque meique,: dum tu ades, sunt oblitae sui,: nec oblitus sui est Ithacus discrimine tanto,was not forgetful of himself, untrue to his nature,; cf. : sui, to forget one's self, know nothing of one's former self, sc. after death, ; also, to forget one's self in a character represented or assumed: tamquam in eo tragoediae argumento sui oblitus tantum Catonem cogitāsset,. —
With gen. of thing: meminens naturae et professionis oblitus,: nec umquam obliviscar noctis illius, etc.,; cf.: oblivisci temporum meorum,: ut nostrae dignitatis simus obliti,: veterumque oblitus honorum,; : oblivisci veteris contumeliae, recentium injuriarum,: controversiarum ac dissensionum,: pristini instituti,: offensarum,: tot exemplorum,.—
With acc. of thing: qui quod dedit id ob litust datum,: officium meum,: injurias,; cf.: artificium obliviscatur,: res praeclarissimas,: totam causam,: haec tam crebra Etruriae concilia,, Drak. N. cr.: ut alia obliviscar,.—With acc. of person: obliti sunt Deum,; .—
With inf.: oblita pharetram tollere,: suas quatere pennas,: dicere aliquid. : obliviscor, Roscium et Cluvium viros esse primarios,.—(ε) With a rel.clause: in scriptis obliviscebatur, quid paulo ante posuisset,.—
Poet., transf., of things: saeclis obliviscentibus,i. e. causing forgetfulness,: oblito pectore,: pomaque degenerant sucos oblita priores, forgetting, i. e. being deprived of losing, ; imitated by Col. poët. 10, 408.—
Prov.: oblivisci nomen suum,to forget one's own name, to have a bad memory,.—
Part. fut. pass.: oblitusque meorum, obliviscendus et illis,: obliviscendi stratiotici,.!*? In Pass. signif. (poet. and late Lat.): post emancipationem in totum adoptivae familiae obliviscuntur,: oblita carmina,; : oblitos superūm dolores,: suis hominibus oblitus,.

la:verb:obligo.gloss: to bind in obligation, obligate, make liable
senses: to bind in obligation, obligate, make liable
la:verb:obligo.html:
ob-lĭgo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
Lit.
To bind or tie around, to bind or fasten to any thing (very rare): obligatus corio,bound in a leathern sack,: articulis muscus obligatus,bound upon,: cibum ovis, to bind or unite with eggs, : amylo spisso obligare,; .—
To bind together, bind up (rare): pecua ad hanc collo in crumena ego obligata defero,: age obliga, obsigna cito, tie up (the letter, in order to seal it), : manipulos,.—
To bind up, bandage, swathe (class., esp. of wounds): crus fractum,: vulnus,; cf.: medicum requirens, a quo obligetur,to bind up his wounds,; : venas,to bandage the veins,: surculum libro,: oculos,: ore obligato obsignatoque simulacrum,.—
Trop.
In gen., to bind, oblige, put under an obligation, make liable, etc. (cf.: obstringo, devincio): aliquem obligare militiae secundo sacramento,bind by a second oath, swear in again,: vadem tribus milibus aeris,to bind in the sum of,: voti sponsio, quā obligamur deo,; : se nexu,: se in acta cujusquam, Tib. ap. : se chirographo ad aliquid,: aliquem sibi liberalitate,to bind to one's self,: obligabis me,will oblige me, lay me under an obligation,; : obligari foedere,: pro amicis alicui obligari, to lay one's self under obligation, i. e. to solicit favors, : obligor ipse tamen,: obligatus ei nihil eram,was under no obligation to him,: me obligatum tibi fore,: obligati sunt interrogatum,.—Poet.: Prometheus obligatus aliti,devoted, condemned to,: ergo obligatam redde Jovi dapem,vowed, due,: obligor, ut tangam laevi fera litora Ponti,am compelled,.—
In partic.
To render liable through guilt, to make guilly: cum populum Romanum scelere obligāsses,: votis caput,: se scelere,: se furti, Scaev. ap. .—Pass., to be guilty of, to commit an offence: est enim periculum, ne aut neglectis iis impiā fraude, aut susceptis anili superstitione obligemur,; cf.: lege Corneliā testamentariā obligatur,offends against,.—
Jurid. t. t.
To bind, engage one (cf. obligatio, II. B.): obligandi, solvendi sui causā,: se obligare,; .—
To pledge, pawn, mortgage a thing: magistratui bona ejus obligantur,: omnia praedia fratri,: omnia bona sua pignori,: nam fundi et aedis obligatae sunt ob amoris praedium,has a mortgage on it,: aedes pignori,: obligata praedia,.—
Transf., beyond the jurid. sphere: obligare fidem suam,to pledge one's word,.—
To impede, restrain, embarrass: judicio districtum atque obligatum esse, .—Hence, oblĭ-gātus, a, um, P. a., bound, obliged: iisdem (officiis) me tibi obligatum fore,.—Comp.: quanto quis melior et probior, tanto mihi obligatior abit,: ipsi obligati sunt,ensnared, embarrassed,.

senses: The state of being forgotten, oblivion.
la:noun:oblivio.html:
oblīvĭo, ōnis, f.
obliviscor
.
Lit., a being forgotten, forgetfulness, oblivion (class.): oblivio veteris belli,: laudem alicujus ab oblivione atque a silentio vindicare,to rescue from oblivion,: meam tuorum erga me meritorum memoriam nulla umquam delebit oblivio,: dare aliquid oblivioni,to consign to oblivion,: oblivione obruere,; for which (late Lat.): oblivioni tradere, , 18, 31, 2; : omnes ejus injurias voluntariā quādam oblivione contriveram,had consigned to oblivion,: in oblivionem negoti venire,to forget,: satius erat ista in oblivionem ire,to be forgotten,: in oblivionem diuturnitate adduci,: capit me oblivio alicujus rei,I forget something,: per oblivionem,through forgetfulness,: in oblivione est,is forgotten,.—In plur.: carpere lividas Obliviones,; ; .—
Transf.
Subject., a forgetting, forgetfulness (post-Aug.): in eo (Claudio) mirati sunt homines et oblivionem et inconsiderantiam,, .—
Concr
Oblivio litterarum, a poet. designation of Orbilius Pupillus, a grammarian, who lost his memory in his old age, Bibacul. ap. .—
Flumen Oblivionis, an appellation of the river Limia, in Hispania Tarraconensis, acc. to the Gr. ὁ τῆς λήθης, ; ; called flumen Oblivio, Liv Epit. 55.

la:verb:oblecto.html:
ob-lecto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
2. lacto
,
to delight, please, divert, entertain, amuse (class.; most freq. with se and mid.; syn. delecto); constr. usually aliquem (aliquid, se), with abl., with cum, with in and abl.
With abl.: ut quam diutissime te jucundā opinione oblectarem,: cum eorum inventis scriptisque se oblectent,: se agri cultione,; : aliquem falso gaudio,: Musae me oblectant carmine,.—With an impers. object: legentium animos fictis oblectare,; so, ironically: paulum praesidii, qui familiarem suam vitam oblectet modo,cheer, comfort,: vitam sordido pane,.—Mid.: in communibus miseriis hac tamen oblectabar speculā,: ludis oblectamur,.—
With cum: oblecta te cum Cicerone quam bellissime,: cum his me oblecto, qui res gestas scripserunt,; cf. elliptically: ego me interea cum libellis,.—
With in: in eo me oblecto,I delight in him, he is my delight,: se in hortis,: ego me in Cumano et Pompeiano satis commode oblectabam,i. e. amused myself excellently well in Cumanum,.—
With acc.: minime equidem me oblectavi,: hortulos emere ubi se oblectare posset,: ut te oblectes scire cupio,: populum,.—With an impers. object: haec studia adulescentiam alunt, senectutem oblectant,; : animos,; : animum,.—
Transf., to spend or pass time agreeably: studio lacrimabile tempus,: iners otium,: inter cenam oblectamus otium temporis,.—
Hence, to delay, detain: ego illum interea hic oblectabo,: dic mi ubi, Philotis, te oblectāsti tam diu,.

la:verb:obluctor.gloss: to struggle against, contend with, oppose
senses: to struggle against, contend with, oppose
la:verb:obluctor.html:
ob-luctor, ātus, 1,
v. dep., to strive or struggle against, to contend with, oppose a person or thing (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.
With dat. of person: soli obluctandum Fabio,to contend with Fabius alone,.—
With dat. of thing: genibusque adversae obluctor harenae,struggle against,: fruticibus,: flumini,. —
Absol.: obluctantia saxa Submovit nitens,.—
Trop.: ut erat animi semper obluctantis difficultatibus,: oblivioni,: morti,.

la:verb:oblino.html:
ob-lĭno, lēvi, rarely lĭni (Varr. ap. P.), lĭtum, 3 (form acc. to the 4th conj. oblinio, q. v.),
v. a., to daub or smear over, to bedaub, besmear (syn.: inficio, induco).
Lit.
In gen.: cerussā malas oblinere,: se visco,: obliti unguentis,: oblitus caeno,: oblitus faciem suo cruore,having besmeared his face with his own blood,: caede,: sanguine,.—
In partic.
To smear over, blot out, rub out any thing written (post-class.; cf.: deleo, interpolo, oblittero): vestrum obleverunt et vestri superscripserunt,.—Trop.: veritatem oblinire,to blot out,.—
To bemire, befoul, defile (syn.: polluo, inquino, maculo): quid tu istuc curas, ubi ego oblinar atque voluter? Lucil. ap. : catulos,: aliquem caeno,; cf. also II. A.—
To stop up by smearing, to plaster over (syn. obturo): dolia oblinito,: amphoram,: oblinitur minimae si qua est suspicio rimae,is stopped up,: gypso oblitus cadus,.—
Transf., to cover over, fill with any thing (of things; very rare): villa oblita tabulis pictis,.—
Trop.
To befoui, defile (class.): se externis moribus. : oblitus parricidio,: sunt omnia dedecore oblita,: geram morem vobis et me oblinam sciens,: aliquem versibus atris,to defame,.—
To cover over, to fill with any thing; to fill to excess, to overload: facetiae oblitae Latio. Roman wit which had received a Latin tincture (through the right of citizenship granted to the Latins), : divitiis oblitus actor,covered, decked,: oblita oratio,overloaded,: Sallustii scripta nimiā priscorum verborum affectatione oblita,.—
To cover over, blind, deceive: sicine mihi esse os oblitum,.

la:verb:obliquo.html:
oblīquo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
obliquus
,
to turn, bend, or twist aside, awry, or in an oblique direction (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: oculos,: visus,: equos,: pedes,: crinem,to draw back,: in latus ensem,: sinus (velorum) in ventum,to turn obliquely to the wind, veer to the wind,.—
Trop.: obliquat preces, makes, utters indirectly, i. e. dissemblingly, : responsa,: Q (littera), cujus similis (litterae K) effectu specieque nisi quod paulum a nostris obliquatur, i. e. is pronounced somewhat softer, *.

senses: In a bad sense, envious, hostile
la:adj:obliquus.html:
oblīquus (oblīcus, v. Orthogr. Vergl. p. 449 Wagner), a, um, adj.
ob and liquus; root lek-; Gr. λέχριος, λέχρις, slantwise (cf.: λοξός, Λοξίας); Lat. licinus, limus, luxus, luxare
,
sidelong, slanting, awry, oblique (freq. and class.; cf.: transversus, imus).
Lit.: motus corporis, pronus, obliquus, supinus,: hos partim obliquos, partim aversos, partim etiam adversos stare vobis,on one side of you, sideways,: obliquo claudicare pede,: sublicae,: ordines,: iter,: obliquam facere imaginem,a side-likeness, profile,: chordae,i. e. of the triangular harp,: verris obliquum meditantis ictum Sanguine donare,: obliquo dente timendus aper,: rex aquarum cursibus obliquis fluens,: radix,: obliquo capite speculari,: non istic obliquo oculo mea commoda quisquam Limat,with a sidelong glance, an envious look,: non obliquis oculis sed circumacto capite cernere,: obliquoque notat Proserpina vultu,.— Adverbial phrases: ab obliquo, ex obliquo, per obliquum, in obliquum, obliquum, from the side, sideways, not straight on: ab obliquo,: nec supra ipsum nec infra, sed ex obliquo,: serpens per obliquum similis sagittae Terruit mannos,: cancri in obliquom aspiciunt,: obliquum, obliquely, askance: oculis obliquum respiciens,.—Comp.: quia positio signiferi circa media sui obliquior est,.—
Fig.
Of relationship, not direct, collateral (poet. and late Lat.): obliquum a patre genus,i. e. not born of the same mother with myself,: obliquo maculat qui sanguine regnum,by collateral consanguinity,; cf.: tertio gradu veniunt ... ex obliquo fratris sororisque filius,.—
Of speech.
Indirect, covert: obliquis orationibus carpere aliquem,: insectatio,: dicta,: verba,.—
In a bad sense, envious, hostile (post-class.): Cato adversus potentes semper obliquus,.—
In gram.
Obliquus casus, an oblique case (i. e. all the cases except the nom. and voc.), opp. rectus: alia casus habent et rectos et obliquos, Müll.—
Obliqua oratio, indirect speech: apud historicos reperiuntur obliquae allocutiones, ut in T. Livii primo statim libro (c. 9): urbes quoque, ut cetera, ex infimo nasci; deinde, etc.,: oratio,.— Hence, adv.: oblīquē, sideways, athwart, obliquely.
Lit. (class.): quae (atomi) recte, quae oblique ferantur,: sublicae oblique agebantur,: procedere. : situs signifer,.—
Trop., indirectly, covertly (post-Aug.): aliquem castigare,: perstringere aliquem,: admonere,: agere,.

la:verb:obloquor.gloss: to speak against someone or something; interrupt a speaker, interject
senses: to speak against someone or something; interrupt a speaker, interject
to sing to, accompany or join in singing
la:verb:obloquor.html:
ob-lŏquor, locūtus, 3, v. dep.
In gen., to speak against a person or thing; to interrupt a speaker; to gainsay, contradict (class.; syn. interpello); constr. with dat. or absol.
With dat.: alicui,: vestra exspectatio, quae mihi obloqui videtur,.—
Absol.: obloquere,: te blaterare atque obloqui? Afran. ap. : ut me et appelles, et interpelles, et obloquare, et colloquare, velim,: ferocissime,.—
In partic.
To sing to, to accompany or join in singing (poet.): non avis obloquitur,: obloquitur numeris septem discrimina vocum,mingles the notes of his lute, accompanies on his lute,.—
To blame, condemn (post-Aug.), ; .—
To rail at, reproach, abuse (poet.): quod nunc gannit, et obloquitur,.

la:noun:oblivium.html:
oblīvĭum, ii, n.
obliviscor
,
forgetfulness, oblivion (poet. and once in Tac. for oblivio; usually in the plur.): oblivia rerum,; so ; : longa oblivia potant,: ducere sollicitae jucunda oblivia vitae,: taedae,: agere oblivia laudis,to forget,: suci, qui patriae faciant oblivia,.— In sing.. sententiam oblivio transmittere, , .

la:adj:oblongus.html:
ob-longus, a, um,
adj., rather long, longish; oblong (not in Cic. or Cæs.): missile telum hastili oblongo,: figura,: folia,.

§ 21: scutula,.—Comp.: foramen oblongius,; .

senses: document that confirms a bond or obligation
la:noun:obligatio.html:
oblĭgātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
.
In gen.
A binding (post-class. and very rare): propter linguae obligationem,because of his being tongue-tied,.—
Trop., an ensnaring, entangling: innocentium,: declinantes in obligationes,evil devices,: in obligatione iniquitatis,.—
In partic., jurid. t. t.
An engaging or pledging, an obligation: est gravior et difficilior animi et sententiae pro aliquo quam pecuniae obligatio,: obligationis onere praetoris auxilio non levabitur,: obligationes ex contractu aut re contrahuntur, aut verbis, aut consensu,.—
Transf., an obligatory relation between two persons, one of whom has a right and the other a duty (the right of the creditor and the duty of the debtor): nunc transeamus ad obligationes: omnis enim obligatio vel ex contractu nascitur vel ex delicto,; cf. sqq.: obligationum substantia in eo consistit, ut alium nobis obstringat ad dandum aliquid, vel faciendum, vel praestandum,; : ex maleficio nascuntur obligationes,: obligatio et constituitur et solvitur,: exstinguitur,: submovetur, et saep.—
The document which confirms this relation, a bond, obligation: pignoris obligatio etiam inter absentes recte ex contractu obligatur,; .

la:noun:oblectamentum.gloss: a source of delight, pleasure, amusement
senses: a source of delight, pleasure, amusement
la:noun:oblectamentum.html:
ob-lectāmentum, i, n.
id.
,
a delight, pleasure, amusement (class.; cf.: voluptas, deliciae); with gen. obj.: requies oblectamentumque senectutis,: oblectamenta puerorum,: oblectamenta et solatia servitutis,: gulae,.—With gen. subj.: rerum rusticarum,

.—Absol.: erat ei in oblectamentis draco serpens,.

la:noun:oblatio.html:
ob-lātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
an offering, presenting, a giving or bestowing gratuitously (post-class.; cf.: donum, munus, votum).
In abstr.: honorum oblationibus,: si forte oblatio ei fiat ejus, quod, etc.,.—
In partic., a bid at an auction: qui ceteros oblatione superavit, Cod. Th. 5, 13, 18.—
In concr., a gift, present: amplissimi ordinis, Cod. Th. 6, 2, 14: si maritus ad oblationem dei uxori donavit,. —
Esp., an offering, sacrifice, ; ; ; .

la:verb:obliviscimini.gloss: second-person plural present active indicative/imperative of oblīvīscor
senses: second-person plural present active indicative/imperative of oblīvīscor

senses: wreaking forgetfulness, furthering the loss of conscience
la:adj:obliviosus.html:
oblīvĭōsus, a, um, adj.
oblivio
.
Lit., that easily forgets, forgetful, oblivious (rare but class.): hos (senes) significat credulos, obliviosos,.—Sup.: homo obliviosissimus,.—
Transf., that produces forgetfulness, oblivious (poet.): Massicus (i. e. sollicitudinum oblivionem afferens),.

la:noun:oblectatio.html:
ob-lectātĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
,
a delighting, delight (a favorite word of Cic.): indagatio ipsa habet oblectationem,: animi,: curarum,: vitae,: requies plena oblectationis fuit,.

la:noun:obliquitas.html:
oblīquĭtas, ātis, f.
obliquus
,
a sidelong or slanting direction, obliqueness, obliquity (post-Aug.), : sigui

feri, .—

Transf., ambiguity: oraculi, P.
